Habitica is a free habit-building and productivity app that uses retro RPG elements to gamify your tasks and goals.

Create an avatar then add tasks, chores, or goals you’d like to work on. When you do something in real life, check it off in the app and receive gold, experience, and items that can be used in-game!

• Automatically repeating tasks scheduled for your daily, weekly, or monthly routines
• Flexible habit tracker for tasks you want to do multiple times a day or only once in awhile

• Guilds let you connect with others that share your interests and goals
• Reminders and widgets to help keep you on track
• Customizable color themes with dark and light mode
• Syncing across devices
—
Habitica is an open-source app run by a small team that’s made better by the work of volunteers who contribute pixel art, translations, bug fixes, and more. If you’d like to contribute, reach out!
Community, privacy, and transparency are important to us. Your tasks are private and we don’t sell your personal data to third parties.

Check out our instagram or twitter(@habitica) for the latest news, announcements, and feature spotlights!

results.description:
A real habit tracker and a real RPG. Not a to-do list with a fantasy skin.

Check off your habits and todos. Your character earns XP, gear and loot, and a hand-built world opens up. About 30 minutes a day, and no grinding to keep up with your real life.

HOW IT WORKS
Track your habits, todos and daily reflections. Every completion earns Stamina, XP, Coins and Rare Essence. Spend them to send your character on adventures, hunt monsters, craft gear and push deeper into the world. A habit tracker first, a deep RPG second. Both halves are real.

HABITS AND TODOS THAT STAND ON THEIR OWN
Built to replace the tracker you use today, not sit beside it.
- Flexible habits with checkboxes, timers and counters
- A full todo system with lists, priorities and reminders
- Effort levels, streaks and daily routines that actually stick
- Analytics and history that reward consistency, not perfection
- Every habit is tied to a skill, so your routine trains your character

A REAL RPG UNDERNEATH
This is where Levla goes deeper than any other gamified habit tracker.
- 17 skills to level across Combat, Utility and Crafting
- Hunt monsters and clear dungeons for loot and rare gear
- Ten equipment slots, from helm to boots to enchanted rings
- Hand-drawn, fully animated characters, not pixels or stock sprites
- Farming: plant seeds, grow crops, use them in Alchemy
- Crafting: forge potions, gear and equipment
- Adventures: send your character on AFK, Idle and IRL runs (1 to 8 hours)
- Exploration: go for a real walk to earn Stamina and level Agility
- Quests, leaderboards and a living map to explore

A REAL ECONOMY
Trade with other players at the Trading Post. Buy and sell gear, materials and rare drops. The market is driven by real people doing real habits, so prices move when the community does.

GUILDS THAT REFLECT YOUR HABITS
Build reputation with in-game Guilds based on the habits you actually keep. Your routines decide where you belong and what you unlock. Earn titles that reflect who you are and what you are working on.

REFLECTIONS
Daily prompts across Gratitude, Growth and Intelligence. Take a moment to check in with yourself. Your character benefits. So do you.

A WORLD WORTH SHOWING UP FOR
Talk to the locals, take on their problems, and explore a hand-built world of towns, mines, docks and dungeons. The more real habits you build, the more of the world opens up.

BUILT DIFFERENT
Levla was built by people who love RPGs and actually use habit trackers. We went through every app in this space and kept hitting the same walls: confusing UX, shallow game design, no real depth. So we built the one we wanted to use.

No gimmicks. No guilt trips. Just a genuinely good habit tracker with an RPG that rewards you for showing up.

If you have ever wished building real habits felt as good as leveling up in a real RPG, this is for you.

Download Levla, build your habits, and level up your life.

Life should be as delightful as playing a game, filled with enthusiasm and zest.

When I was fresh out of university, I dove into TED Talks, seeking life's purpose and fresh perspectives. A talk titled "Games Change the World" caught my eye. "Aren't games just for fun?" This revelation made me think. Often, we abandon activities like running or reading because immediate gratification is missing. Our minds crave instant rewards. I designed this app to mirror the instant feedback of games, fuelling your journey towards achieving goals and cementing good habits.

If Sisyphus got upgrades and rewards every time he pushed his boulder, perhaps his task wouldn't seem so endless?

Your to-do list, played like a tabletop RPG. Finish a task, roll the dice, and the total becomes credits you spend on rewards you wrote yourself. Suddenly "reply to emails" is worth a proper coffee.

HOW THE DICE WORK
• Give each quest a complexity: d4 for trivial, d20 for legendary
• Finish it and Questly rolls that die — the total is your credits
• Log focus sessions on a quest first and you roll extra dice, up to six
• Land the same face on every die and a jackpot multiplies the payout

A SHOP YOU STOCK YOURSELF
Rewards are yours to invent. "A lazy Sunday morning", "that game on my wishlist", "a proper coffee" — set a price in credits and cash it in once you've earned it. Credits are only ever earned by finishing quests and checking in on habits: they cannot be bought, and nothing in Questly costs real money except the subscription described below.

HABITS AND STREAKS
Any repeating event can become a habit. Check in on the days you planned to roll for credits, and every consecutive check-in nudges your chance of a bonus die a little higher. Miss a day and the streak resets — unless you are holding a rest token, which is spent automatically to cover the gap.

results.description:
Maintaining productive and healthy habits is a matter of survival. Well, in real life it's not quite that dramatic, but with Skillix we hope to turn mundane routines into something more exciting.
Your daily walk is now a scavenging mission. Your weekend cleaning turns from a simple chore into a way to develop the camp. Every run, study session, programming practice, and completed routine develops your character, builds your settlement, grows your resources, extends your streak - and, most importantly, strengthens your habits.
How does it work? Simple. First, you pick the 'skills' - activities like walking, running, studying, cleaning - that you want to turn into habits (we're constantly adding new skills based on community suggestions). Next, you start a mission while starting the associated activity in real life. Based on the time spent on the activity - and the associated mission - you level up your character and earn resources for your settlement.
Skillix is a gamified RPG productivity app and habit builder, designed around self-discipline. You complete missions in a post-apocalyptic setting where your fully customizable character and settlement grow alongside your own focus and consistency.

-- What makes Skillix different --
There are plenty of other great productivity apps on the market that use gamification, some of which we have used ourselves. We simply decided to build Skillix differently, with more emphasis on the time you spend on activities, different gameplay mechanics and an ethical approach.
• Actual in-game progress powered by your daily productivity: every skill you train earns you EXP and resources;
• You start with a camp that, over time, grows into a thriving settlement;
• Your character is fully customizable, with many body and clothing options;
• We created a unique post-apocalyptic survival setting without grim themes, violence, or heavy stuff. Instead, we went for relaxing, uplifting, warm tones.

-- Our development rules --
Skillix was created by a privacy lawyer, which is part of why we have always maintained certain ethical principles during development.
• No pay-to-win - you can't buy progress. No unethical monetization. No dark patterns nudging you to spend.
• Core functionality is free, forever. You can purchase a Skillix+ subscription to help us develop the app further, but that's entirely optional. You can also earn premium currency (for customization items) just by playing and progressing.
• All designs and art are created entirely by humans. Outside of that, we use AI only for inspiration, research and proof-reading, with extensive human review.
• No intrusive, manipulative, or personalized ads. You can turn ads off completely (and unlock extra bonuses) with Skillix+, which costs about as much as a coffee per month.
• Genuinely privacy focused. Don't want an account? You don't need one. And if you make one, you can delete it (along with every bit of data tied to it) anytime. We do not sell your personal data. We do not build advertising profiles from your habits.

-- Freshly launched --
After 2.5 years of hard work and a successful Kickstarter campaign, we finally launched Skillix in June 2026. We're improving it quickly with community feedback, so bug reports and suggestions are genuinely welcome!
Found something rough around the edges? Have an idea for a better feature, mission, or reward? Please send us feedback through the in-app form (Settings > Support) or join our Discord community (Settings > Community).
Whether you are trying to get more active, build a study routine, practice programming, or just want a game that rewards real-life effort, Skillix gives you a reason to show up every day.

Free to play, so come try it out :)

This is the only app that can turn self-development into a fascinating game! 

If you can relate to this:

- I have wanted to quit smoking/start training/learn foreign language for ages.
- I lack motivation to finish what I started.
- I am always finding excuses.
- I cannot even make myself begin.

… this is the app you need!

How it works:

- You set a goal and a deadline.
- The app represents your goal by a character who runs to the finish line. You have three free characters.
- As the deadline comes close, you should honestly tell if you have achieved the goal.
- If you fail, your character dies.
- You can buy a VIP character; that may help your motivation become financial as well!
- You can score points and spend them to buy the VIP character, too; it could be very painful to lose that one as well :)

Why does it work?
We often put off personal goals because we don’t lose anything if we fail; everything just stays as it is. A more strict deadline and possible tangible loss may dramatically increase your motivation.

What stops you from telling a lie in response to the question, “Has this goal been achieved?”
We assume that you are already tuned to self-motivation; that’s why you can accept the rules of the game. The general rule is to reply honestly no matter the circumstances are. Otherwise, there is no point in the game.

The app will not complete your tasks for you, but create necessary conditions and keep you motivated to achieve what you have in mind. The rest is up to you!

Join the app's Facebook page and share your experience and achievements!

results.description:
Build Habits Slowly is a habit tracker that empowers you to take control of your habits.

===

Why track your habits?

The author of "Atomic Habits," summarizes the benefits of a habit tracker as follows:

1. "It creates a visual cue that can remind you to act."
2. "It is motivating to see the progress you are making. You don’t want to break your streak."
3. "It feels satisfying to record your success in the moment."

This is an excerpt from the article, https://jamesclear.com/habit-tracker. I recommend reading the article if you are interested in habit formation (Build Habits Slowly is not affiliated with Atomic Habits or James Clear, I just found this article informative).

===

What sets Build Habits Slowly apart from other habit trackers?

I created BHS because there were two things that bugged me about using other habit trackers:

1. Losing my momentum at the start of a new month

Most habit trackers display your progress on a monthly calendar page. I found that when I started a new month it was harder for me to continue a habit, because the new month no longer showed all of my habit completion days from the previous month. I had lost a visual indicator of my momentum.

Build Habits Slowly solves this problem by displaying your habit progress in a scrolling calendar "feed." When a new month starts, you still see the days in the previous month(s). So, you never lose the visual sense of momentum as you check off your habits.

2. Streaks breaking after one missed day

Most habit trackers break your habit streak after you miss one day. I found this frustrating, because it's normal to miss a day here or there; life gets in the way of your habits. When I was trying to build a new habit and inevitably missed a day, my streak would break and halt my momentum. This felt demoralizing, because I was setting unreasonable expectations for myself.

Build Habits Slowly solves this problem by giving you the power to decide how many "slip days" you want to give yourself before your streak breaks. For daily habits, I've found that one slip day is perfect for me. This gives me enough flexibility to miss a day, but keeps me motivated to not miss two days in a row.

=

Admittedly, these two problems are pretty small, but they were enough to drive me to create my own habit tracker app. I hope you find Build Habits Slowly as helpful as I have!

results.description:
PointBook is a habit tracker where every routine or goal you check off gives you points to redeem for treats you pick yourself. Say reading for 20 minutes earns 150 points and a movie night costs 5,000. You set both numbers.

Points aren't real money, so you can't turn them into cash or gift cards.

Most days you'll only need the Today tab. It lists the routines due today, each with its current streak and the days it repeats. When you've done one, tap it and the points are added to your total. If that was a mistake, a second tap undoes it any time before midnight, as long as you haven't used those points yet.

Goals have their own card on the Today tab, below your routines. A goal is a one-time thing, like finishing a book or renewing your passport. You can give it a deadline if you like, and if the date passes, the goal just stays on your list.

The Rewards tab lists your rewards by cost, lowest first. For the ones you're still working toward, you'll see how many more points you need and a bar that fills up as you get closer. Your next reward is also on the Today tab, and a Redeem button appears there once you have enough. Before you confirm, PointBook tells you what you'll have left, and you can undo a redemption until midnight. A reward stays on your list after you redeem it, so movie night can happen again.

To add a routine or goal, tap the + on the Today tab. Routines can repeat every day, on weekdays, on weekends, or only on the days you pick. You can set a reminder for each one, and it won't bug you on days off or after you've already checked the routine off.

Streaks only count the days a routine is scheduled, so days off don't break them. If you miss one scheduled day, the streak keeps going, and the Missions tab will tell you which day it was. Miss two in a row and the streak starts over. You never lose points for missing a day.

On the Missions tab, each routine has a row of dots for this week, with a colored dot for every day you did it. Tap History at the bottom for charts of your completions and points over the last 7, 30, or 90 days, or all time. There's also a calendar and a heatmap of the past year. Pick any day on the calendar to see what you did.

There are two Home Screen widgets. The small one has your points, your longest current streak, and how many of today's routines you've done. The medium one lists up to two routines you haven't done yet, and on iOS 17 or later you can tap one to check it off.

You don't need an account, and there are no ads. Your routines, goals, points, and rewards are saved on your device. There's no cloud sync, so before you switch to a new iPhone, export a backup file in Settings and import it on the new one.

PointBook follows your phone's light or dark mode, or you can pick one in Settings. It's available in 12 languages: English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Italian, German, Polish, Korean, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Thai, and Indonesian.

If you're new to this, start with one or two routines and one reward you actually want. When you first open PointBook, you can load a few sample routines and change them from there.
